bibliography.author: Michael A. Jalandoon
bibliography.title: Heavy metals and physico-chemical assessment of water, sediments, and Oreochromis niloticus (Tilapia) in Maragondon River, Philippines
bibliography.thesisCitedByLaterStudy: Jalandoon, M.A. (2018). Heavy metals and physicochemical assessment of water, sediments and Oreochromis niloticus (Tilapia) in Maragondon River, Philippines. Master's thesis, De La Salle University–Dasmariñas.

method: Reviewed the publisher's July 2019 issue page and indexed text from its publisher-hosted article PDF, including the title, study summary, sampling description, and laboratory appendix. The 2024 Maragondon River tilapia paper's bibliography was checked for the original 2018 thesis citation. No local copy was retained; the DLSU-D thesis itself was not located in its public repository during this review.

sourceClaim.samplingPeriod: January–March 2018, as indexed in the article's methods text
sourceClaim.support: The article title, study summary, and laboratory appendix name Oreochromis niloticus tissues from Maragondon River. The accessible text did not establish a voucher/catalog identifier or a diagnostic identification method for the sampled fish.
sourceClaim.taxonomicCrosscheck: Oreochromis niloticus is a recognized species name; name validity does not verify the identity of these study specimens.

comparison.finding: A later primary study at Maragondon River reports Tilapia sp. and explicitly withholds species resolution because of possible interspecific hybridization and uncertainty in the feral fish gene pool.
comparison.interpretation: The later study does not disprove the earlier identification, but it leaves the 2018 species-level claim without independent confirmation. Retain both source labels and the difference in taxonomic resolution; do not resolve the samples to Oreochromis niloticus.

reuse.publisherPageDescription: The issue page labels the edition Open Access.
reuse.copyrightNotice: The same page displays © 2019 Global Scientific Journal. All Rights Reserved.
reuse.decision: No item-specific reuse license or permission was verified. Do not reproduce the paper, tables, figures, or its study-derived species claim in public Bangwit content.

limitations: This is a historical research claim, not evidence of present-day occurrence or a complete river checklist.
No voucher specimen, collection catalog ID, expert determination, or diagnostic identification method was independently verified for the fish named Oreochromis niloticus.
A later 2024 study reported Tilapia sp. and explained why it withheld species resolution; this review does not decide whether the earlier fish were correctly identified.
No item-specific reuse terms were verified despite the issue page's Open Access label.
No study reach geometry, georeferenced stations, salinity classification, abundance, catchability, safety, diet, or fishing legality is established here.
nextAction: Keep this claim held. Seek the original thesis and its taxonomic protocol or voucher evidence through already public institutional sources; verify reuse terms before any redistribution. Continue other CALABARZON leads without treating this candidate as admitted species evidence.
